mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in the federal funds rate signals an easing monetary cycle that compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the unemployment rate below 3.5% indicates a strong labor market, which leads to increased consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the unemployment rate falls below 3.5% but the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of the next 20-day periods.

mechanism_narrative: When payroll employment increases by more than 200,000 and the unemployment rate decreases, it signals a strong labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If payroll employment increases by more than 200,000 and unemployment decreases, but the S&P 500 does not show positive returns in more than 50% of the next 20-day periods.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in real personal consumption expenditures (PCE) adjusted for inflation indicates strong consumer demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If real PCE increases but the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of the next 60-day periods.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production indicates increased economic activity, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If industrial production increases but the S&P 500 does not show positive returns in more than 50% of the next 60-day periods.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in housing starts indicates strong demand in the housing market, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If housing starts exceed 1.6 million but the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of the next 20-day periods.

mechanism_narrative: When real personal consumption expenditures (PCE) increase and the consumer price index (CPI) remains stable, it indicates strong demand without inflationary pressures, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If real PCE increases and CPI remains stable but the S&P 500 does not show positive returns in more than 50% of the next 60-day periods.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the federal funds rate above 2.0% indicates a tightening monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the federal funds rate rises above 2.0% but the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 40% of the next 20-day periods.
